description: §66.12.6 rule 1 (a struct field whose type is a tape carries its grants) + rule 3 (tape methods are named after their grants) + §66.10 (aliases snapshot): `b.xs.append(…)` / `b.xs.pop()` edit the tape FIELD of a `const` struct local, judged by the field's type `int[free, append, pop]`; the edit rebinds no name (RULED S475), and `before`, taken from `b.xs` before the edits, keeps its one element. One #go click sets @n to 2 * 10 + 1 = 21.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S469 "⭐ RULED — NO unconstrained sequence behaviour anywhere in the language" ("No position escapes the grant check. That covers locals, parameters, returns, struct fields, tuple positions …"); ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S475 "⭐ RULED — local tape edit on a `const` local or parameter is an EDIT" ("read as edit")
rationale: §66.12.6 rule 1: "a struct field whose type is a tape (§66.11.4: the field's tape type carries its grants)"; rule 3: `xs.append(x)` is granted by `append`, `xs.pop()` by `pop`. §66.10 rule 1: "A binding … initialized from … any value holds a snapshot of that value", so `before` is unchanged by the later edits.
